title: Speech of President Arroyo during the 1st Laguna Investment and Business Expo
text:
Speech of Her Excellency Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo President of the Philippines During the 1st Laguna Investment and Business Expo

[Delivered at the Event Center, SM Sta. Rosa, Sta. Rosa City, Laguna, November 04, 2008]

Thank you, Secretary Lazaro. Maraming salamat sa pagpakilala mo sa akin at maraming salamat sa inyong pag-imbita sa akin at sa mga Cabinet members na dumalo dito.

Mayor Arcillas Nazareno, congratulations din! Congressman Dan Fernandez, Congressman Evie Arago, siyempre si President Mamon ng Laguna Chamber otherwise known as Mr. Enchanted Kingdom, (applause) at ang ating mga Cabinet members na napakaraming narito and the national agencies. Congratulations on this Investment and Business Expo! (Applause)

This Expo demonstrates a vibrant private-public sector partnership. And held in the midst of the global economic storm, it also demonstrates that the Philippines is in relatively good shape. Gaya nga nang sabi ni Ning Lazaro kanina nung kami ay nakaupo, “Eh tignan niyo naman ang Laguna parang walang global crisis.” Congratulations sa Laguna! (Applause)

Laguna has carved out a name as the industrial area with perhaps the widest array of investment venues in what we call the Luzon Urban Beltway. And it is also part of the Cyber Corridor. In fact, one reason why Rey Chua is here, our ICT chair, together with Larry and Peter, is that we are proud to congratulate Metro Laguna, made up of Sta. Rosa, Calamba, San Pablo, Cabuyao and Los Baños, as having been selected by the Business Process Outsourcing Association as the next wave city’s, number one after Metro Manila. (Applause) So, it is indeed a part of the Cyber Corridor as well.

And it is also one of the nation’s major rice producing provinces. So, talagang microcosm ang Laguna ng buong bansang Pilipinas.

But today, we’re talking about the Luzon Urban Beltway, the Cyber Corridor — dalawa sa ating limang natural sub-economies or “super regions” of the Philippines kung saan gumagastos tayo ng daan-daang bilyon sa ilalim ng ating Medium-Term Public Investment Program.

The Luzon Urban Beltway consists of most of Central Luzon, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Mindoro and Marinduque. And if it has to be a good urban beltway, it must be globally competitive for urban service and industrial sectors with a high quality of life for its people. And indeed, this Luzon Urban Beltway produces more than one-half of the country’s Gross Domestic Product.

To be globally competitive in our Medium-Term Philippine Development Plan we invest in five strategic measures:

Eh kita naman niyo yung SLEX inaayos natin at pagkatapos nito yung SLEX ikakabit sa STAR. At yung SLEX nakakabit sa C-5 ay ikakabit sa NLEX. So, lahat nito ay pag-uusapan mamaya sa ating Cabinet meeting which we are holding here in Sta. Rosa, Laguna. (Applause)

Yung logistic is movement of people and goods. So, kasama dito yung gastos sa pagbiyahe at kasalukuyan, sabi ni Secretary Larry Mendoza sa akin, ay may hearing na ginaganap ang LTFRB para pag-usapan kung papano bumaba ang pasahe dahil bumababa ang presyo ng langis.

Pero ang gusto kong pag-usapan ngayon to reduce the cost of electricity in the urban beltway, PEZA now offers reduced rates for the locators. And the implementation of open access awaits the consummation of the Calaca investment in the power sector. Inaasahan natin na ito ay matapos ng Nobyembre. At ang hinihintay naman ng Calaca ay yung desisyon ng Energy Regulatory Commission tungkol sa pwedeng ma-icharge na mga power generating plants.

Earlier than this, we began the “Time of Use” method of computing power rates along with the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market and MERALCO’s Customer Choice Program and High Load Factor Discounts for consumers that are consuming at least 5 megawatts. Loans of electric cooperatives have been condoned. And recently, the ERC ruled that the system’s loss recovery cannot be more than 8 percent.

Mamaya sa ating Cabinet meeting ay pag-uusapan rin kung papano pa tayo makakababa ng ating energy cost lalo na para sa SME at para sa karaniwang Pilipino.

Your government is doing everything in its power to put food on the table, dahil ang busog na empleyado ay hindi parating hihingi ng omento sa kanyang sweldo. And to protect the paycheck therefore from high prices and high inflation, we are also continuing to invest in our nation’s system of healthcare, education and social services.

Because the relative strength and resilience of our people and our economy is still no consolation to the Filipino who has to pay higher prices for basic commodities, we are aware of the pressures you face from high prices and high rates of inflation. We know that you, especially those employees and professionals, are concerned about job security and the buying power of your wages and salaries. We are also concerned.

That is why we are working hard to keep down the prices of rice, food and fuel, and to increase the number of jobs and investments that will continue to generate high-paying employment opportunities for more of our countrymen. Kaya kami ng Cabinet ay nagpunta dito dahil itong Expo ay malaking kontribusyon dito sa paghanap ng marami pang investment.

Yung mga magsasaka naman, they’re getting the investments they need. The government will continue its unprecedented support for agriculture via the F.I.E.L.D.S. program. NFA will buy one million metric tons from Filipino farmers compared to last year’s less than 100,000 metric tons. In fact, sabi ni Arty Yap sa akin, to date 330,000 metric tons na ang nabili ng NFA compared to 30,000 the last time around. Sana ang ating magsasaka, dahil marami sa kanila maganda ang presyong natatanggap mula sa NFA, ay magtanim pa ng higit pang palay.

And with this, we expect inflation, which has started to come down, to come down even more. And the price of rice, which has started to come down, should go down even more. And with that, we expect the earning power of your workers and officers’ paycheck to increase.

Our economic team, eto si Peter, is working to rein in inflation — kasi Peter is a member of the Monetary Board — and to monitor prices. Yun nga ang trabaho niya kasama ng local government bilang DTI Secretary and put the price manipulators out of business.

He and we will continue to make spot checks in markets to make sure no one is taking advantage of their fellow citizens during this challenging time. Pero itong challenging time na ito ay nakakapag Expo pa rin ang Laguna.

This Expo — Congratulations to all of you! — (applause) this Expo makes me optimistic about our future. It makes me optimistic about the hope–optimism and resilience of the people of Laguna.

Mahalagang layunin nitong Expo na patunayan ang kagalingan ng probinsiyang Laguna bilang sentro ng pamumuhunan at negosyo. Nagsisilbi din siyang patunay ng kahusayan, kagandahan, kahandaan at tibay ng loob ng mga taga-Laguna sa pagsulong ng kaunlaran.

So, for playing such an important role in our country’s economy, maraming salamat sa inyong lahat.

Thank you. (Applause)
